assistant|route_recommendation_golden_ga: Golden Gate Bridge to Sausalito: scenic route with views of the bridge, Alcatraz, and Marin Headlands
assistant|route_recommendation_dumbarton: Dumbarton Bridge Loop: a 30-mile loop across Dumbarton Bridge through Fremont and Newark back to the East Bay
assistant|route_recommendation_san_mateo: San Mateo County Coast: scenic coastal route through Half Moon Bay, Pescadero, and Santa Cruz
assistant|route_recommendation_mount_tam: Mount Tamalpais: a challenging climb with views of the Bay Area and the Pacific Ocean
assistant|route_recommendation_berkeley_: Berkeley Hills: a scenic loop through the Berkeley Hills with views of the Bay
assistant|carbon_wheel_price_range: Carbon fiber wheels typically range from $1,000 to $5,000 or more depending on brand and quality
assistant|derailleur_tip_barrel_adjuster: Turn barrel adjuster clockwise to increase cable tension, counterclockwise to decrease; start 1-2 turns clockwise from fully loose
assistant|derailleur_tip_cog_clearance: In the largest cog, derailleur should have about 1-2 mm of clearance from the cassette
assistant|bike_computer_recommendation_g: Garmin Edge series recommended: offers GPS, heart rate monitoring, and performance tracking
assistant|bike_computer_recommendation_w: Wahoo Elemnt series recommended: offers GPS, heart rate monitoring, and cycling app integration
assistant|bike_computer_recommendation_l: Lezyne Super GPS recommended: compact, affordable device with GPS, heart rate monitoring, customizable screens
assistant|derailleur_tip_limit_screws: Check the L and H limit screws; too loose risks shifting into the spokes, too tight makes shifting difficult
assistant|derailleur_tip_alignment: Ensure the derailleur is parallel to the cassette and the hanger is straight; adjust or replace a bent hanger
assistant|derailleur_tip_smallest_cog: Shift into the smallest cog (11- or 12-tooth) and check the derailleur is not rubbing the cassette
assistant|largest_cog_size: The largest cog is typically 25- or 28-tooth; verify 1-2 mm derailleur clearance
assistant|derailleur_tip_chain_length: Check chain length; a chain that is too long can cause shifting issues
assistant|derailleur_tip_fine_tune: Shift through all gears and fine-tune the barrel adjuster so the chain moves smoothly without skipping or rubbing
assistant|route_planning_tools: Use Strava, Ride with GPS, or MapMyRide to find popular routes; local bike shops and cycling clubs are also good sources
assistant|ride_safety_essentials: Wear appropriate gear and bring water, snacks, and a basic tool kit on rides
assistant|century_prep_tires: Replace tires if they are more than 6-12 months old or have been used extensively
assistant|century_prep_drivetrain: Check the chain for wear and stretch and inspect the cassette for wear; replace as needed
assistant|century_prep_brake_pads: Check brake pads for wear and replace if worn down for reliable braking on long rides
assistant|century_prep_cables: Inspect brake and gear cables for fraying or rust and replace if necessary
assistant|century_prep_wheel_bearings: Check wheel bearings for smooth rotation and play; service or replace if rough or loose
assistant|century_prep_frame_fit: Inspect frame and fork for damage, ensure all bolts are tightened, and check saddle and handlebar comfort
assistant|century_ride_training_nutritio: Gradually increase mileage and intensity before the ride; plan nutrition and hydration with energy bars, gels, and water
assistant|century_ride_pacing_support: Start at a comfortable pace and maintain it; consider riding with a group or a support vehicle
assistant|bike_maintenance_habits: Regularly clean and lubricate the chain, derailleurs, and other components to prevent wear and corrosion
assistant|bike_management_tips: Designate a primary bike, rotate maintenance, keep a bike journal, and set a bike budget
assistant|century_prep_tune_up: Get the road bike serviced by a professional mechanic before the century ride
assistant|bike_computer_features: Consider GPS accuracy, heart rate monitoring, data tracking, customization, app integration, battery life, and water resistance
assistant|phone_mount_options: Cases from Lifeproof or Quad Lock; mounts from Quad Lock or Rokform; weather-resistant pouches from Aquapac or H2O Audio
assistant|carbon_wheel_pros: Carbon fiber wheels are lighter, stiffer, more aerodynamic, and absorb road vibrations for a smoother ride
assistant|carbon_wheel_cons: Carbon fiber wheels are expensive, prone to damage from debris or crashes, and may need specific brake pads
